story.title: Haley Stevens Endorses Mike Rogers Following Withdrawal from El-Sayed Event
story.summary: Haley Stevens has publicly endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for the Michigan Senate seat after being disinvited from an event by Abdul El-Sayed's campaign due to a dispute over an antisemitic advertisement. This endorsement marks a significant shift in the race, potentially impacting El-Sayed's campaign as polls tighten in the final days before the election.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed in Stevens’s position?
explore_lenses.title: From backing the ticket to endorsing Rogers
explore_lenses.summary: Haley Stevens had recently said she would vote for Abdul El-Sayed, but on November 1 she publicly endorsed his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, after El-Sayed’s campaign asked her not to attend its remaining events.

claims.text: Stevens announced that she was endorsing Rogers after saying El-Sayed had told her she was no longer welcome in his campaign and should stay away.

The shift followed Stevens’s recent public statement that she would vote for El-Sayed, making the Rogers endorsement a break from her prior general-election position rather than merely an appearance with him.
Stevens’s endorsement does not change the ballot or remove El-Sayed as the Democratic nominee; it is a political signal to voters.

explore_lenses.label: What do Stevens, El-Sayed and Rogers argue?
explore_lenses.title: A dispute over an outside ad and campaign focus
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate dispute concerns an advertisement made by Rebellion PAC, not by El-Sayed’s campaign. Stevens said the ad was antisemitic and demanded a stronger response; El-Sayed rejected its content and said the conflict was distracting from voter issues; Rogers praised Stevens’s intervention.

claims.text: The Rebellion PAC ad linked U.S. military aid to Israel with grocery costs; El-Sayed’s campaign said it was not affiliated with the ad, and El-Sayed said he did not agree with its contents.
Stevens characterized the ad as antisemitic and pressed El-Sayed to condemn it; she also criticized his broader framing of Israel-related spending and Michigan domestic needs.
El-Sayed said Stevens was trying to relitigate the Democratic primary and said he did not want the dispute to distract from the campaign’s central issues.
Rogers praised Stevens for raising concerns voiced by Michigan Jewish voters, framing her intervention as principled rather than simply partisan.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the Senate race?
explore_lenses.title: Voting ends November 3; canvassing follows
explore_lenses.summary: Michigan’s general election is scheduled for November 3, 2026. The remaining campaign period is short, and formal canvassing deadlines extend beyond election night.

claims.text: Michigan lists November 3, 2026 as the upcoming general-election date; its constitutionally required early in-person voting period ran from October 24 through November 1.

Michigan’s election calendar sets November 6 as the deadline to cure a signature problem on an absent-voter ballot return envelope and November 9 as the deadline for timely postmarked military and overseas ballots to be received and counted.
County canvassing boards must complete their November general-election canvasses by November 17, and the Board of State Canvassers has until November 23 to meet to canvass the election.

Forecast: AP described the contest as tightly contested and potentially relevant to Senate control, so both campaigns are likely to focus on turnout rather than further procedural changes before Election Day.

story_report.summary: Former Democratic candidate Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan’s U.S. Senate race after saying Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed told her she was no longer welcome in his campaign and should stay away. The break followed a dispute over an advertisement that Stevens described as antisemitic. Stevens had recently said she would vote for El-Sayed, making her backing of Rogers a reversal of her earlier general-election position. The endorsement leaves El-Sayed on the ballot as the Democratic nominee but gives Rogers a high-profile political signal to voters.

sections.heading: Advertisement Dispute Divides Democratic Rivals
sections.body: The dispute centered on a Rebellion PAC advertisement that linked U.S. military aid to Israel with grocery costs. El-Sayed’s campaign said it was not affiliated with the ad, and El-Sayed said he did not agree with its contents. Stevens pressed El-Sayed to condemn the spot and criticized his wider framing of Israel-related spending and Michigan domestic needs. El-Sayed said Stevens was seeking to relitigate the Democratic primary and that he did not want the disagreement to distract from the campaign’s central issues.

sections.heading: Rogers Seeks Support From Stevens
sections.body: Rogers praised Stevens for raising concerns he said were voiced by Michigan Jewish voters, portraying her intervention as principled rather than merely partisan. Her endorsement is a departure from her prior pledge to vote for El-Sayed, but it does not alter the candidates listed on the ballot. The practical effect will depend on whether Stevens’s move changes voter behavior in a contest described as tightly contested and potentially consequential for Senate control.

sections.heading: Michigan Election Certification Timeline
sections.body: Michigan’s general election is scheduled for Nov. 3, 2026, after early in-person voting ran from Oct. 24 through Nov. 1. Voters have until Nov. 6 to cure signature problems on absent-voter ballot envelopes, while timely postmarked military and overseas ballots may be received and counted through Nov. 9. County canvassing boards must finish their canvasses by Nov. 17, and the state canvassing board has until Nov. 23 to canvass the election.

related_stories.title: Federal Judge Dismisses Trump's Lawsuit to Block Alaska Senate Race Certification
related_stories.summary: A federal judge has dismissed a lawsuit from the Trump administration that sought to block the certification of results from Alaska's U.S. Senate race, contingent on the Republican incumbent losing. The state government of Alaska had argued against the lawsuit, calling the demands 'impossible.'

related_stories.title: Alaska Attorneys Reject Trump's Request to Set Aside Senate Ballots as 'Meritless'
related_stories.summary: Attorneys for Alaska have described Trump's demand to set aside Senate ballots as 'meritless' and 'not even possible.' This statement comes amid a broader investigation by the Department of Justice, which has issued subpoenas related to the case. Additionally, there is a request for a judge to separate ballots showing votes for a specific candidate until it can be determined if voters were misled into voting for a spoiler candidate.

related_stories.title: Ciara Mageean, European Champion Runner, Dies at 34 After Cancer Battle
related_stories.summary: Ciara Mageean, the Irish Olympian and European 1,500m champion, has passed away at the age of 34 after a battle with cancer. Mageean, who represented Ireland in two Olympic Games, revealed her cancer diagnosis a year prior to her death. Tributes have been paid from various figures, including President Catherine Connolly.
